GROSS WARP for Ableton Live (Max for Live)
==========================================

Half time, tape stops, stutters, rolls, scratches, reverses and gates, drawn as two
envelopes and locked to your song.

In this folder
--------------
  Gross Warp.amxd        the effect (a Max audio effect)
  Gross Warp MIDI.amxd   optional: plays Gross Warp's patterns from MIDI notes (a Max MIDI effect)
  gw_ui.js               the effect's editor - keep it in the same folder as Gross Warp.amxd
  INSTALL.txt            this file

You need Ableton Live 12 Suite, or Live 12 Standard with the Max for Live add-on.


Install
-------
1. Unzip GrossWarp.zip. You get a folder called "Gross Warp".

2. Put the folder where Live can see it - either way works:
   a) Move it into your User Library:
        macOS:    ~/Music/Ableton/User Library/
        Windows:  C:\Users\<you>\Documents\Ableton\User Library\
      (Live > Settings > Library shows where your User Library is.)
   b) Or leave it anywhere and, in Live's browser, click "Add Folder..." under Places
      and choose the "Gross Warp" folder.

3. In Live's browser open User Library (or the folder you added) > Gross Warp, and drag
   "Gross Warp" onto an audio track, a drum rack, a group or the Master.

4. Press Play. Gross Warp follows Live's transport; while Live is stopped it passes the
   sound through untouched.

Keep the three files together: Gross Warp.amxd loads gw_ui.js from its own folder. To
make one self-contained file for sharing, click the wrench in the device's title bar
(opens Max), click the snowflake (Freeze), and save it under a new name.


Play
----
- Pads 1-8 pick the pattern (it is the Pattern parameter: automate it). Alt-click
  (Option-click on Mac) a pad to copy the shown pattern into it.
- Time / Volume picks the envelope you draw. Blue = time: top is normal, lower plays
  later; a fall at 45 degrees stops, steeper plays backwards, steps repeat a slice.
  Orange = volume.
- < preset > steps through presets; click the name for the browser (categories and
  Combos that set both envelopes).
- Click to add points, drag them, Alt-click or double-click to delete, drag the small
  circles to bend a line. Shift = no snapping. The bars icon paints steps.
- Dice rolls a new pattern (Shift-click: change one envelope). Flip turns the envelope
  upside down. Copy / Paste work between Gross Warps.
- Switch: when a new pattern starts (Now, 1/16, Beat, Bar, end of Pattern).
- Hold loops a short slice (< > set 1/16 to 1 bar). Swing: drag up/down.
- # (grid): snap and pattern Length (1 beat to 4 bars, any time signature).
- Gear: Hold Last/Next, Grain size, MIDI link, Evolve (changes the pattern as it plays).
- Pitch Lock keeps the pitch while the time envelope slows, stops or reverses the
  sound.


Trigger patterns from MIDI (optional)
-------------------------------------
1. Make a MIDI track and drag "Gross Warp MIDI" onto it.
2. Set its Link (A) and, on Gross Warp, set MIDI to the same letter.
3. Notes from Base (C1) up: C1 = pattern 1, C#1 = 2, ... G1 = 8.
   Mode Hold: the pattern plays while the note is held, then Pattern takes over again.
   Mode Latch: a note switches to its pattern; the same note again releases it.
   Mode One-shot: a note plays its pattern once, then Pattern takes over again.
4. Draw the notes in a MIDI clip, or arm the track and play them. They follow Switch.
Several Gross Warps on the same link all follow the same notes.


If something is off
-------------------
Open Max's console: click the wrench in the device's title bar (Max opens), then
Window > Max Console, and look for red lines.
- "can't find file gw_ui.js": the script isn't next to Gross Warp.amxd.
- A gen~ error: please send me the line.
- Nothing happens while Live is stopped: that's by design.
